signatures.name: Karpenter does not support the cluster Kubernetes version
signatures.pattern: failed validating kubernetes version|validating kubernetes version, karpenter( version)? is not compatible with (K8s|kubernetes) version
signatures.meaning: The Karpenter controller considers the EKS Kubernetes version outside its supported range (MinK8sVersion..MaxK8sVersion of the provider). Up to v1.0.x this is the "failed validating kubernetes version" error line; from v1.1.0 it is the error field of the version controller's "Reconciler error". The nodeclass.status controller stops resolving AMIs, so new nodes do not launch or launch only with old AMIs.
signatures.cause: EKS was upgraded without upgrading the Karpenter chart (or vice versa), or 1.x version validation is on and the patch version is outside the support table.
signatures.verify: kubectl logs -n karpenter -l app.kubernetes.io/name=karpenter --since=24h | grep -c 'validating kubernetes version'; helm list -n karpenter

signatures.name: Spot or capacity-reservation interruption notice
signatures.meaning: EC2 announced it will reclaim a spot node in 2 minutes and Karpenter deleted the NodeClaim ("initiating delete from interruption message" with messageKind spot_interrupted, SpotInterruptionKind on 0.37.x). signatures.cause: Spot market fluctuation. The narrower the instance types, the more frequent.

noisy.note: The noisy-neighbour verdict is left to the LLM (type: llm, tenancy.noisy-neighbor). If node saturation minutes are 0, no neighbour could have done harm. Only nodes where a dominant namespace, saturation and prod throttling on the same node overlap are candidates.

summary.max_pods_rule: normal when max-pods <= IP limit + 2 (allowance for hostNetwork pods)

vpccni.note: ip_max is the value reported by ipamd (otherwise computed as ENI count x (IPv4 per ENI - 1)). assigned is the number of IPs ipamd handed to pods, so hostNetwork pods are not included. no_available_ip_events accumulates since the process started.

ndots.note: With the default ndots:5, an external name with fewer than 5 dots (api.example.com) is first tried with <ns>.svc.cluster.local, svc.cluster.local, cluster.local and the VPC search domain appended, producing 3-4 NXDOMAINs before the real name is asked. That is why the NXDOMAIN ratio is high and the query count is several times the number of real names. Fixes: trailing dot (FQDN), ndots:2, or the autopath plugin

kubeproxy.note: On k3s, kube-proxy runs inside the k3s process, so there is no DaemonSet or ConfigMap and its metrics appear mixed into the kubelet scrape (instance :10250, :6443). rules_pending_s = queue time − sync time (0 if negative). iptables_rules is 'the number of rules written in the last sync', so after a partial sync (seen on EKS 1.32: nat 5) it is not the full scale — judge scale by services and endpoints

credentials.note: Without a dedicated role the controller uses the node instance role's EC2 permissions — every pod on the node shares them (together with the IMDS hop)

karpenterctl.note: Metrics accumulate since the leader process started. NodePool/NodeClaim details are in summary.scaling.karpenter
